technical_and_design_decisions: Adopt standard Spring Boot auto-configuration conventions for Spring Cloud Stream (s-c-s) modules migrated from Spring XD.
Utilize Cloud Foundry Java Client v2 for refactoring the CC SPI deployer to standardize deployment calls and reactive status monitoring.
Implement multi-binder routing via Spring Cloud Stream binder abstractions to support runtime binding of Rabbit, Redis, and Kafka modules.
Use Spring Boot externalized configuration mechanisms (property sources and environment overrides) to handle Maven coordinate overrides for modules.
assumptions: Development will occur on Java 8 compatible toolchains given the target framework versions (Spring 4.2.1, SI 4.2, AMQP 1.5).
Target repositories (s-c-s, Spring XD, modules repo) are accessible with existing CI/CD build scripts.
All work including design, implementation, unit testing, and integration verification will be performed by a single software engineer.

activities.activity_description: Migrate Kafka and Rabbit modules from Spring XD to s-c-s repository as sink components (U1, U2), and relocate header-enricher module to XD proper (U7), including package updates and module build alignment.
Implement channel binding infrastructure to dynamically configure and swap Rabbit, Redis, and Kafka binders for source and sink channels (U3).
Develop dynamic module configuration override support allowing external config files to override default module resolution properties and Maven coordinates (U4).
Refactor Cloud Foundry SPI deployer using CF Java Client library to replace legacy REST/custom deployer code, improving deployment lifecycle reliability and performance (U5).
Add flexible Hadoop distribution configuration to dynamically load distribution-specific libraries into the classpath at runtime (U6).
Upgrade core dependencies to Spring Framework 4.2.1, Spring Integration 4.2, and Spring AMQP 1.5, resolving breaking API changes and deprecations across the project (U8).
Conduct end-to-end testing across multi-binder deployments, CF SPI deployer scenarios, and regression tests for updated framework dependencies.
